title: Body Leveling in Wheel-Legged Obstacle Traversal with Residual PPO
author: Junxian Zhu
affiliation: Mechanical Engineering and Materials Science · Duke University
intro: A wheel-legged robot crosses a step. Recording captures the reference motion; Residual PPO adds learned corrections to help keep the body more level.

videos.title: 100 mm · the matched nominal case
videos.conditions: 100 mm step · 218.5 mm initial gap target · friction scale 1.000
videos.model: Updated 100 mm model · learned wheel-gain head_04 + frozen joint policy
videos.watch: Follow the chassis, especially from 30–53 s. Then watch the posture changes around 54–65 s.
videos.result: Both methods complete. Body-tilt RMS is lower with the updated PPO controller; large posture changes still occur and peak tilt is almost unchanged.

videos.title: 50 mm · the historical reference
videos.conditions: 50 mm step · 218.5 mm initial gap target · friction scale 1.000
videos.model: Older frozen 50 mm policy · separate from the updated 100 mm model
videos.watch: Compare body inclination as each wheel transfers onto the step. This is one successful example.
videos.result: Both methods complete this case. Across the separate 39-condition historical suite, common completion was 39/39 for Recording and 28/39 for PPO; this clip does not establish higher reliability.

videos.title: 100 mm · a longer initial gap
videos.conditions: 100 mm step · 238.5 mm initial gap target · friction scale 1.000
videos.model: Updated 100 mm model · same head_04 as the nominal case
videos.watch: Watch how the approach and wheel transfers change when the starting gap is 20 mm longer.
videos.result: Both methods complete. The gap differs from the nominal clip, so compare the two methods within this video rather than comparing finish times across videos.

videos.title: 100 mm · a useful counterexample
videos.conditions: 100 mm step · 207.7 mm initial gap target · friction scale 1.176
videos.model: Updated 100 mm model · same head_04 as the successful clips
videos.watch: Follow the PPO side through 57.73 s, then keep watching the Recording side finish.
videos.result: PPO terminates with a logged body-collision failure; Recording succeeds. The earlier-ending side holds its final measured pose. This clip alone does not identify the causal mechanism.
